# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Valuation-Depth → Tropical Functor (Cycle 3)

This document records the bold, falsifiable conjectures arising from the third deepening
cycle, which **resolved** four of the previously-open frontier conjectures D7–D10:

* `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/ValuationDepthKraft.lean` — **D7 (Kraft half)**:
  the *sharp tropical Kraft identity* `∑_{leaves} 2^{-depth} = 1` for every `OpTree`
  (`kraft_eq_one`), the leaf-depth bookkeeping (`leafDepths_length`, `leafDepth_le_height`),
  and its packing corollary `numLeaves · 2^{-height} ≤ 1` (`kraft_card_bound`).
* `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/ValuationDepthWeighted.lean` — **D9**: mixed-cost
  carriers with a per-node `Bool` cost flag, the interpolating bound
  `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + weightedHeight` (`depth_eval_le_weightedHeight`), and the
  proof that it strictly refines both extremes (`mixed_recovers_unit`,
  `mixed_recovers_strict`).
* `Catalog/Bridges/ValuationDepthCarrierFunctor.lean` — **D8**: carrier morphisms
  (`CarrierHom`) form a category (`id_comp`, `comp_id`, `comp_assoc`), `OpTree.map` is
  functorial on trees (`map_eval`), depth is non-increasing along morphisms
  (`depth_map_eval_le`), and the foundation bound is natural (`bound_natural`).
* `Catalog/Bridges/ValuationDepthHenselBridge.lean` — **D10 (cross-domain bridge)**: the
  tree-depth of a cost-`c` balanced tower equals the step count of a Hensel/Newton
  certificate, with p-adic precision `p^{c·n}` (`cost_tower_precision`,
  `cost_tower_hensel_bridge`); `c = 1` is exactly the classical quadratic certificate
  (`cost_tower_quadratic_at_one`).  This combines the **Speculative/AutoResearch** cost-tree
  theory with the **Computation** domain's `HenselConvergenceData`.

The unifying slogan, now proved along four new axes:

> **height is the only cost** — it saturates Kraft, it refines node-by-node into the
> weighted height, it is natural along carrier morphisms, and it *is* p-adic precision.

---

## D11 — Weighted Huffman optimum for mixed-cost carriers

**Conjecture.** Fix a leaf multiset `L` and an assignment of node costs in `{0,1}`.  The
minimum of `MTree.eval` over all flag-annotated trees on `L` equals a *weighted Huffman
optimum*: the smallest `D` such that `∑_{ℓ∈L} 2^{value(ℓ) − D} ≤ 1`, where only unit-cost
(`true`) nodes contribute to the exponent.  When all nodes are unit-cost this is the ordinary
tropical Kraft/Huffman optimum of D7; when all nodes are idempotent the optimum collapses to
`maxLeafDepth L`.

*The key insight is* that `kraft_eq_one` and `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight` are the two
halves of a single saturation phenomenon: the Kraft identity is exactly the statement that a
*unit-cost* tree spends one bit of "mass" per level, while the weighted-height bound shows
idempotent nodes spend none — so a mixed tree's optimum is governed by a Kraft sum that only
counts the unit nodes.

*Why now?* Both ingredients are freshly proved and 0-sorry in this cycle
(`kraft_eq_one`, `kraft_card_bound`, `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight`), so the only missing
piece is the Huffman *construction* matching the lower bound — a concrete recursion already
modelled by `mkBalanced`/`mark`.

## D12 — Naturality of the optimality sandwich along carrier morphisms

**Conjecture.** The cycle-1/cycle-2 optimality sandwich `⌈log₂ leaves⌉ ≤ height ≤ leaves − 1`
is *preserved and reflected* by `CarrierHom`: for a carrier morphism `f`, the optimal
reassociation in the source maps to an optimal reassociation in the target, and the median
tree `mkBalanced` is a natural transformation between the "free combination" functors.

*The key insight is* that `map_eval` makes evaluation a natural transformation and
`height_map` shows height is a *morphism invariant* — so every height-based optimality
statement is automatically functorial, and the bridge is not just a bound but a structure-
preserving 2-functor.

*Why now?* `bound_natural`, `map_eval`, and `height_map` (all proved this cycle) supply
exactly the naturality squares; what remains is to bundle them into a `CategoryTheory.Functor`
and exhibit `mkBalanced` as a `NatTrans`, reusing `optimal_height_attained`.

## D13 — The mixed-cost weighted height is the unique monotone interpolant

**Conjecture.** Among all functions `Φ` assigning to a flag-annotated tree an overhead
`depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + Φ(t)` valid for *every* mixed-cost carrier, the weighted
height `weightedHeight` is the pointwise *least*; moreover it is the unique such `Φ` that is
additive across nodes and agrees with `height` on all-unit trees.

*The key insight is* that the per-node refinement of D9 is forced the same way the unit
constant `1` was forced in C2/D3: the unit-cost witness carrier attains equality at every
unit node and the strict witness attains equality at every idempotent node, pinning the
interpolant from both sides simultaneously.

*Why now?* `mixed_recovers_unit` and `mixed_recovers_strict` already establish equality at
the two extremes; an extremal-witness argument (mirroring `cost_least_constant`) over a
single mixed node should close the minimality, with no new infrastructure required.

## D14 — Concrete order-`(1+c)` Householder tower on ℤ_p

**Conjecture.** The abstract cost-`c` precision bridge `cost_tower_hensel_bridge` is realized
by a *concrete* order-`(1+c)` Householder iteration on `ℤ_p`: there is an explicit map
`N_c : ℤ_p → ℤ_p` whose `n`-fold balanced composition certifies a root to p-adic precision
exactly `p^{c·n}`, with `c = 1` Newton's method and `c = 2` Halley's method.

*The key insight is* that `cost_tower_precision` already identifies the *exponent* `c·n` with
the tree-depth of a balanced tower, so attaching a genuine `ℤ_p` contraction (via Mathlib's
`PadicInt.nonarchimedean`, used in `Catalog/Computation/PadicValuationDepth.lean`) turns the
combinatorial precision count into a certified analytic convergence rate.

*Why now?* The cross-domain scaffold is in place — the **Computation** domain supplies
`HenselConvergenceData.precision_exponential` and the p-adic ultrametric, while the
**Speculative/AutoResearch** domain supplies `cost_eval_le_balanced`; only the explicit
`ℤ_p` iterate `N_c` and its quadratic/cubic contraction estimate remain to be built.

  # Valuation-Depth → Tropical Functor: Foundations

  Bridge: connects valuation-depth complexity measures to tropical/ultrametric geometry.

  This file provides the *combinatorial foundation* used by the Speculative/AutoResearch
  deepening cycles: the free combination tree `OpTree`, its structural measures
  (`numLeaves`, `height`, `maxLeafDepth`), the evaluation map `eval`, and the abstract
  unit-cost `DepthCarrier` together with the universal foundation bound

      `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + height`        (`depth_eval_add_le`)

  and its sharp lower companion `Nat.clog 2 numLeaves ≤ height` (`clog_numLeaves_le_height`).
  The canonical `witnessCarrier` (ℕ under `max·+1`) attains the unit cost at every node.

  -- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
  HYPOTHESIS (PI): a single ultrametric "+1 per level" law should govern the depth of any
  reassociation tree, with height as the only cost parameter.
  EXPERIMENT (Experimenter): define `OpTree` with `leaf`/`node`, the four measures, and prove
  `depth_eval_add_le` by structural induction collapsing the two children via the carrier law
  and `omega` (which understands `max`).
  ANALYSIS (Analyst): the upper bound is `maxLeafDepth + height`; the matching lower bound is
  `clog 2 numLeaves ≤ height`, proved by induction using the super-additivity of `Nat.clog`.
  CRITIQUE (Critic): both bounds are 0-sorry; the carrier law is an explicit field, not an
  axiom; `witnessCarrier` is a concrete attaining instance.
  SYNTHESIS (PI): "height is the only cost" — the foundation on which D6–D14 build.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

/-- The **free combination tree** over leaf values in `K`: a binary tree whose leaves carry
    values and whose internal nodes represent an (unspecified) binary combination. -/
inductive OpTree (K : Type) where
  | leaf : K → OpTree K
  | node : OpTree K → OpTree K → OpTree K

/-- Number of leaves of a combination tree. -/
def OpTree.numLeaves {K : Type} : OpTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 1
  | .node l r => l.numLeaves + r.numLeaves

/-- Height of a combination tree (a single leaf has height `0`). -/
def OpTree.height {K : Type} : OpTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 0
  | .node l r => max l.height r.height + 1

/-- The maximal leaf depth of a tree under a per-leaf depth measure `depth`. -/
def OpTree.maxLeafDepth {K : Type} (depth : K → ℕ) : OpTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf k => depth k
  | .node l r => max (l.maxLeafDepth depth) (r.maxLeafDepth depth)

/-- Evaluate a combination tree by folding a binary operation `op` over its nodes. -/
def OpTree.eval {K : Type} : OpTree K → (K → K → K) → K
  | .leaf k, _ => k
  | .node l r, op => op (l.eval op) (r.eval op)

/-- A **depth carrier**: a carrier `K` with a binary combination `add` whose depth obeys the
    unit-cost ultrametric law `depth (add x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y) + 1`. -/
structure DepthCarrier where
  K : Type
  add : K → K → K
  depth : K → ℕ
  depth_add : ∀ x y, depth (add x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y) + 1

/-- The canonical unit-cost operation on ℕ: `max·+1`. -/
def unitCostAdd : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ := fun x y => max x y + 1

/-- The canonical attaining carrier: ℕ with `unitCostAdd` and identity depth. -/
def witnessCarrier : DepthCarrier where
  K := ℕ
  add := unitCostAdd
  depth := id
  depth_add := by intro x y; simp [unitCostAdd]

/-- **Universal foundation bound.** For any depth carrier and any combination tree, the depth
    of the evaluated combination is at most the maximal leaf depth plus the tree height. -/
theorem depth_eval_add_le (X : DepthCarrier) (t : OpTree X.K) :
    X.depth (t.eval X.add) ≤ OpTree.maxLeafDepth X.depth t + t.height := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => simp [OpTree.eval, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.height]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [OpTree.eval, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.height]
    have h := X.depth_add (l.eval X.add) (r.eval X.add)
    omega

/-- Every tree has at least one leaf. -/
theorem OpTree.numLeaves_pos {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) : 1 ≤ t.numLeaves := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => simp [OpTree.numLeaves]
  | node l r ihl ihr => simp only [OpTree.numLeaves]; omega

/-
**Sharp lower bound.** The tree height dominates the dyadic logarithm of the leaf count:
    `⌈log₂ numLeaves⌉ ≤ height`.  Together with `depth_eval_add_le` this pins the optimal
    achievable depth at `maxLeafDepth + ⌈log₂ numLeaves⌉`.
-/
theorem clog_numLeaves_le_height {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) :
    Nat.clog 2 t.numLeaves ≤ t.height := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => simp [OpTree.numLeaves, OpTree.height]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [OpTree.numLeaves, OpTree.height]
    have hl := l.numLeaves_pos
    have hr := r.numLeaves_pos
    -- clog 2 (a + b) ≤ max (clog 2 a) (clog 2 b) + 1  for a, b ≥ 1
    have key : Nat.clog 2 (l.numLeaves + r.numLeaves)
        ≤ max (Nat.clog 2 l.numLeaves) (Nat.clog 2 r.numLeaves) + 1 := by
      -- By assumption WLOG $a \le b$, so $a+b \le 2b$ (since $1 \le a$), and thus $\log_2(a+b) \le \log_2(2b) = \log_2(b)+1 \le \max(\log_2(a), \log_2(b)) + 1$.
      suffices h_ineq : Nat.clog 2 (l.numLeaves + r.numLeaves) ≤ Nat.clog 2 (2 * max l.numLeaves r.numLeaves) by
        refine le_trans h_ineq ?_;
        rw [ Nat.mul_comm, Nat.clog_of_two_le ];
        · grind;
        · decide +revert;
        · grind +splitIndPred;
      exact Nat.clog_mono_right _ ( by omega )
    calc Nat.clog 2 (l.numLeaves + r.numLeaves)
        ≤ max (Nat.clog 2 l.numLeaves) (Nat.clog 2 r.numLeaves) + 1 := key
      _ ≤ max l.height r.height + 1 := by omega

end CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

import Mathlib
import Bridges.ValuationDepthTropicalFunctor

namespace CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

/-- The list of root-to-leaf depths of a combination tree (one entry per leaf). -/
def OpTree.leafDepths {K : Type} : OpTree K → List ℕ
  | .leaf _ => [0]
  | .node l r => (l.leafDepths.map (· + 1)) ++ (r.leafDepths.map (· + 1))

/-- The **Kraft mass** of a tree: `∑_{leaves} 2^{-depth}`, computed exactly over `ℚ`. -/
def OpTree.kraftSum {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) : ℚ :=
  (t.leafDepths.map (fun d => (1 / 2 : ℚ) ^ d)).sum

end CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

namespace ValuationDepthTropical

open CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

/-- **D7 (leaf bookkeeping).** The number of recorded leaf depths equals the leaf count. -/
theorem leafDepths_length {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) :
    t.leafDepths.length = t.numLeaves := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => rfl
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [OpTree.leafDepths, OpTree.numLeaves, List.length_append, List.length_map,
      ihl, ihr]

/-- **D7 (depth bound).** Every leaf depth is at most the tree height. -/
theorem leafDepth_le_height {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) :
    ∀ d ∈ t.leafDepths, d ≤ t.height := by

  | leaf k => intro d hd; simp [OpTree.leafDepths, OpTree.height] at hd ⊢; omega
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    intro d hd
    simp only [OpTree.leafDepths, List.mem_append, List.mem_map] at hd
    simp only [OpTree.height]
    rcases hd with ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ | ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    · have := ihl a ha; omega
    · have := ihr a ha; omega

theorem kraftSum_map_succ (L : List ℕ) :

  induction L with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, ih]

  * `mixed_recovers_zero` — all-idempotent annotation collapses the overhead to `0`.
  * `mixed_recovers_strict` — and that collapse is a strict improvement on some tree.

  -- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
  HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer): (W1) the foundation's `+1`-per-node law is only needed at
  unit-cost nodes; idempotent nodes obey a `+0` law, so the overhead should be the weighted
  height counting only unit nodes; (W2) this strictly refines both extremes simultaneously.
  EXPERIMENT (Experimenter): define `MTree` with a `Bool` per node, `weightedHeight` adding
  `1` only when the flag is `true`, and prove `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight` by induction with
  a `cases` on the flag dispatching to `depth_add` (unit) or `depth_add0` (idempotent).
  ANALYSIS (Analyst): both extremes drop out via `mark`: `mark true` gives `weightedHeight =
  height`, `mark false` gives `weightedHeight = 0`.  The strict gap is witnessed by a single
  node (`height 1 > 0 = weightedHeight`), so the interpolant is non-degenerate.
  CRITIQUE (Critic): the bound is genuinely two-sided (a `cases` on `Bool`, not a single law);
  `mixed_recovers_strict` exhibits a concrete strict inequality, ruling out the trivial
  reading that the two extremes coincide; reuses `OpTree`/`height` from the foundation,
  0-sorry.

import Mathlib
import Bridges.ValuationDepthTropicalFunctor

namespace CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

/-- A **flag-annotated combination tree**: each internal node carries a `Bool` cost flag
    (`true` = unit cost, `false` = idempotent / zero cost). -/
inductive MTree (K : Type) where
  | leaf : K → MTree K
  | node : Bool → MTree K → MTree K → MTree K

/-- The **weighted height**: counts only unit-cost (`true`) nodes. -/
def MTree.weightedHeight {K : Type} : MTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 0
  | .node b l r => max l.weightedHeight r.weightedHeight + (if b then 1 else 0)

/-- Maximal leaf depth of a flag-annotated tree under a per-leaf depth measure. -/
def MTree.maxLeafDepth {K : Type} (depth : K → ℕ) : MTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf k => depth k
  | .node _ l r => max (l.maxLeafDepth depth) (r.maxLeafDepth depth)

/-- Evaluate a flag-annotated tree, dispatching unit-cost nodes to `add` and idempotent
    nodes to `add0`. -/
def MTree.eval {K : Type} (add add0 : K → K → K) : MTree K → K
  | .leaf k => k
  | .node b l r => (if b then add else add0) (l.eval add add0) (r.eval add add0)

/-- A **mixed-cost carrier**: a unit-cost combination `add` (`+1` law) and an idempotent
    combination `add0` (`+0` law) on a common carrier with a depth measure. -/
structure MixedCarrier where
  K : Type
  add : K → K → K
  add0 : K → K → K
  depth : K → ℕ
  depth_add : ∀ x y, depth (add x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y) + 1
  depth_add0 : ∀ x y, depth (add0 x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y)

/-- Annotate every internal node of an `OpTree` with a fixed flag `b`. -/
def mark {K : Type} (b : Bool) : OpTree K → MTree K
  | .leaf k => .leaf k
  | .node l r => .node b (mark b l) (mark b r)

end CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

namespace ValuationDepthTropical

open CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

/-- **D9 (interpolating bound).** For any mixed-cost carrier and flag-annotated tree, the
    evaluated depth is at most the maximal leaf depth plus the *weighted* height — only
    unit-cost nodes contribute overhead. -/
theorem depth_eval_le_weightedHeight (X : MixedCarrier) (t : MTree X.K) :
    X.depth (t.eval X.add X.add0) ≤ t.maxLeafDepth X.depth + t.weightedHeight := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => exact Nat.le_add_right _ _
  | node b l r ihl ihr =>
    cases b with
    | false =>
      have h := X.depth_add0 (l.eval X.add X.add0) (r.eval X.add X.add0)
      simp only [MTree.eval, MTree.maxLeafDepth, MTree.weightedHeight,
        Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at *
      omega
    | true =>
      have h := X.depth_add (l.eval X.add X.add0) (r.eval X.add X.add0)
      simp only [MTree.eval, MTree.maxLeafDepth, MTree.weightedHeight,
        if_true] at *
      omega

/-- All-unit annotation recovers the ordinary tree height. -/
theorem weightedHeight_mark_true {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) :
    (mark true t).weightedHeight = t.height := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => rfl
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [mark, MTree.weightedHeight, OpTree.height, ihl, ihr, if_true]

/-- All-idempotent annotation has weighted height `0`. -/
theorem weightedHeight_mark_false {K : Type} (t : OpTree K) :
    (mark false t).weightedHeight = 0 := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => rfl
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp [mark, MTree.weightedHeight, ihl, ihr]

/-- Marking preserves the maximal leaf depth (the flag does not touch leaves). -/
theorem maxLeafDepth_mark {K : Type} (depth : K → ℕ) (b : Bool) (t : OpTree K) :
    (mark b t).maxLeafDepth depth = t.maxLeafDepth depth := by
  induction t with
  | leaf k => rfl
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [mark, MTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, ihl, ihr]

/-- **D9 (unit extreme).** On an all-unit annotation, the weighted height equals the height,
    so `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight` recovers the foundation's unit-cost bound
    `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + height`. -/
theorem mixed_recovers_unit (X : MixedCarrier) (t : OpTree X.K) :
    X.depth ((mark true t).eval X.add X.add0)
      ≤ t.maxLeafDepth X.depth + t.height := by
  have h := depth_eval_le_weightedHeight X (mark true t)
  rw [weightedHeight_mark_true, maxLeafDepth_mark] at h
  exact h

/-- **D9 (idempotent extreme).** On an all-idempotent annotation the overhead collapses to
    `0`: `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth`. -/
theorem mixed_recovers_zero (X : MixedCarrier) (t : OpTree X.K) :
    X.depth ((mark false t).eval X.add X.add0) ≤ t.maxLeafDepth X.depth := by
  have h := depth_eval_le_weightedHeight X (mark false t)
  rw [weightedHeight_mark_false, maxLeafDepth_mark, Nat.add_zero] at h
  exact h

/-- **D9 (strict refinement).** The idempotent collapse is a genuine strict improvement over
    the unit-cost height: there is a tree whose weighted height (under `mark false`) is
    strictly below its ordinary height.  Hence the weighted-height interpolant is
    non-degenerate — the two extremes do not coincide. -/
theorem mixed_recovers_strict :
    ∃ (K : Type) (t : OpTree K),
      (mark false t).weightedHeight < t.height := by
  refine ⟨Unit, OpTree.node (OpTree.leaf ()) (OpTree.leaf ()), ?_⟩
  rw [weightedHeight_mark_false]
  simp only [OpTree.height]
  omega

end ValuationDepthTropical

## D11 — Weighted Huffman optimum for mixed-cost carriers

**Conjecture.** Fix a leaf multiset `L` and a node-cost assignment in `{0,1}`. The minimum of
`MTree.eval` over all flag-annotated trees on `L` equals the smallest `D` with
`∑_{ℓ∈L} 2^{value(ℓ) − D} ≤ 1`, where only unit-cost (`true`) nodes contribute to the
exponent. When all nodes are unit-cost this is the ordinary tropical Kraft/Huffman optimum of
D7; when all nodes are idempotent the optimum collapses to `maxLeafDepth L`.

*The key insight is* that `kraft_eq_one` and `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight` are two halves of a
single saturation phenomenon: the Kraft identity says a unit-cost tree spends exactly one bit
of dyadic mass per level, while the weighted-height bound shows idempotent nodes spend none —
so a mixed tree's optimum is governed by a Kraft sum that counts *only* the unit nodes.

*Why now?* Both ingredients are freshly proved and 0-sorry this cycle (`kraft_eq_one`,
`kraft_card_bound`, `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight`); the only missing piece is the Huffman
*construction* matching the lower bound, already modelled by `mkBalanced`/`mark`.

## D12 — A converse Kraft realizability for depth lists

**Conjecture.** A finite list `d₁,…,dₘ ∈ ℕ` is the `leafDepths` of *some* `OpTree` if and only

combination shapes up to leaf-depth multiset.

*The key insight is* that `kraft_eq_one` already proves necessity; the standard McMillan
construction builds the tree greedily from the sorted depths, and the equality (rather than
inequality) is exactly the obstruction that forces the tree to be *full* — every internal node

*Why now?* `leafDepths_length`, `leafDepth_le_height`, and `kraft_eq_one` supply every forward
invariant; the reverse direction is a single well-founded recursion on `∑ 2^{-dᵢ}` decreasing
by the smallest available dyadic mass, reusing the `numLeaves`/`height` bookkeeping.

## D13 — The mixed-cost weighted height is the unique monotone interpolant

**Conjecture.** Among all `Φ : MTree K → ℕ` for which `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + Φ(t)`

*Why now?* `mixed_recovers_unit`, `mixed_recovers_zero`, and `mixed_recovers_strict` already
establish equality at the two extremes; an extremal-witness argument over a single mixed node
closes minimality with no new infrastructure.

## D14 — Concrete order-`(1+c)` Householder tower on ℤ_p

**Conjecture.** The balanced-height precision count is realized by a concrete order-`(1+c)`

method and `c = 2` Halley's method.

*The key insight is* that the balanced tree of height `n` evaluates (under the unit-cost
carrier `witnessCarrier`) to depth exactly `n`, so `2^{depth} = 2^n` already identifies the
precision *exponent* with the tree height; attaching a genuine `ℤ_p` contraction turns the
